==English==

===Etymology===
{{ety|en|:bor|de:homosexual|tree=1}}
Borrowed from {{bor|en|de|homosexual}}, from {{m|de|homo-|t=same}} + {{m|de|sexual|t=relating to sex or sexuality}}, coined by {{w|Karl Maria Kertbeny}} in 1868, and popularized in {{w|Richard von Krafft-Ebing}}'s ''{{w|Psychopathia Sexualis}}'' (2nd ed. 1887, in German) and {{w|Charles Gilbert Chaddock}}'s 1892 English translation thereof (compare {{m|en|bisexual}}), displacing the slightly older term {{m|en|Uranian}}.<!-- Now itself partially displaced by {{m|en|gay}} and {{m|en|queer}}, see usage notes.--> Equivalent to {{affix|en|homo-|-sexual}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{a|en|RP}}:
** {{IPA|en|/ˌhɒməʊˈsɛksjuːəl/|/ˌhɒməʊˈsɛkʃuːəl/}}
** {{IPA|en|/ˌhəʊməʊˈsɛksjuːəl/|/ˌhəʊməʊˈsɛkʃuːəl/}}
** {{audio|en|en-uk-homosexual.ogg|a=UK}}
* {{a|en|US}}:
** {{enPR|hō'mə-sĕkʹsho͞o-əl|hō'mō-sĕkʹsho͞o-əl}}, {{IPA|en|/ˌhoʊməˈsɛkʃuːəl/|/ˌhoʊmoʊˈsɛkʃuːəl/}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-homosexual.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɛkʃuəl|ɛkʃuːəl|s=5}}
* {{hyph|en|ho|mo|sex|ual}}

===Adjective===
{{en-adj}}

# {{lb|en|of a person or other animal|formal|distancing|or|dated}} Sexually and/or romantically attracted to members of the same sex, such as a man who is attracted to other men or a woman who is attracted to other women; [[gay]]. {{qualifier|Typically used in the sense of sole/exclusive attraction.}}
#: {{usex|en|No, it wouldn't make a difference if the applicant was '''homosexual'''.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1892|page=97|tlr=Charles Gilbert Chaddock
|title=Psychopathia Sexualis|url=https://archive.org/details/psychopathiasexualis00kraf/page/96/mode/2up
|location=Philadelphia
|publisher=F. A. Davis
|original=Psychopathia Sexualis
|by=R. von Krafft-Ebing
|origyear=1889
|passage=[H]e said he had never noticed anything '''homosexual''' in himself.}}
# {{lb|en|of a romantic or sexual act or relationship|formal|distancing|or|dated}} Between two people of the same sex; [[gay]].
#: {{usex|en|Most western countries have repealed laws against '''homosexual''' activity between consenting adults.}}
# {{lb|en|dated}} Intended for or used by homosexuals, ''as'' a [[nightclub]], a [[bar]], etc.

====Usage notes====
* Many style guides<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20191227131845/https://www.glaad.org/reference/style GLAAD media reference guide], citing the AP and NYT style guides.</ref> and many gay people<ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/2014/03/23/fashion/gays-lesbians-the-term-homosexual.html?mcubz=1 NYT article]</ref> recommend against the use of the word "homosexual" because of its clinical and sometimes pejorative connotations, preferring the terms {{m|en|gay}} and (for women) {{m|en|lesbian}}, and relationship descriptors like "same-sex relationship". Many consider it particularly pejorative when it is used as a noun, and prefer "gay man", "gay woman" (or "lesbian").
* The first part of the word derives from the Greek word for "same", which is traditionally pronounced {{IPAchar|/ˈhɒməʊ/}}, unlike the Latin word {{m|la|homo||man, human being}}<!-- (semantically contrast {{m|la|vir||man, male}})-->, which is pronounced {{IPAchar|/ˈhəʊməʊ/}} (RP). However, it is much more common to pronounce the first vowel as {{IPAchar|/əʊ/}} (RP) / {{IPAchar|/oʊ/}} (US) than as {{IPAchar|/ɒ/}}.

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# {{senseid|en|Q101922089}} {{lb|en|typically|formal|distancing|or|dated}} A person who is sexually attracted solely or primarily to others of the same sex.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1936
|title=Suriname folk-lore
|author=w:Melville J. Herskovits
|author2=Frances S. Herskovits
|location=New York
|publisher=Columbia University Press
|page=32
|url=https://www.dbnl.org/tekst/hers005suri01_01/hers005suri01_01_0010.php
|text=It must not be understood that homosexuality is confined to women. Relationships of this type exist also among men, and in ''[[Sranan Tongo|taki-taki]]'' are to be found words which are specific designations for male '''homosexuals''', who are termed ''hantimąn'', or ''awɛge''.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260828042049/https://www.dbnl.org/tekst/hers005suri01_01/hers005suri01_01_0010.php|archivedate=28 August 2026}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1963|author=John Rechy|title=City of Night|page=48
|passage=Soon, we got up, walked around the west side — toward the "[[meat rack]]" — the gay part of the park. There, it was as if someone had hung a line of marionettes on the railing: the lonesome young '''homosexuals''', legs dangling, looking, waiting for that one-night's sexual connection...}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1997|journal=The Advocate|issue=742|page=9
|passage=It was unheard-of for those of us who are 30-something or older to have had an openly gay role model when we were young. '''Homosexuals''' weren't depicted in the media in a positive light, if at all.}}

====Usage notes====
* "Homosexual" as a noun is more often applied to males while females are more likely to be described as [[lesbian]]s.
* Many style guides and gay people advise against the use of "homosexual" as a noun; see the usage notes above.

====Synonyms====
* This section is divided into two tables, one containing synonyms that generally are not derogatory and one containing those that generally are. However, note that the non-derogatory terms can nonetheless be used derogatorily, and that some of the derogatory ones are often used humorously and non-derogatorily by gay people and others.
